evaluations.label: A
errors: 'Strong support for a dedicated lounge/reading room' overstates it: Susan asked 'Do we really need that?' and Martin questioned its use
'Majority lean toward a mixed-use room' is not supported; Martin said it was an open discussion with no decision
'Andrei and Agnès negotiate a merged solution' slightly overstates; the transcript says Andre and Agnes will discuss it with the other group
strengths: Captures key numbers correctly (15 people, ~18 positions, 16 slots if a 2P room becomes the reading room, zero growth)
Correct attributions (Susan wants own office for confidential rectorate work; Martin open to sharing but on the phone a lot)
Most complete next-steps list: room separation, 4 desks in a 3P room, Gisela with the school admin, Maggie and Pierrette, draft proposals, Tuesday 2 PM after the MDM meeting
Clear, well organized, easy to act on
weaknesses: Next steps have no owners (e.g. Susan volunteered to ask Maggie and Pierrette; Andre to check room separation)

evaluations.label: B
errors: 'accommodate approximately 15 to 18 people' is wrong; there are 15 people and about 18 positions

'noting this is common in other faculties but not necessarily here' reverses the transcript: Andre said sharing with assistants is common at the school, Susan said other faculties all have their own offices
'Action Items (none)' is wrong; Andre committed to check room separation and Susan to ask Maggie and Pierrette, and everyone was asked to bring proposals
'Members were tasked with consulting colleagues, such as Maggie and Pierrette' misattributes; Susan volunteered for that
Lounge described as 'a significant requirement... to serve as a meeting or overflow space' while its purpose was explicitly left open
strengths: Lists the unresolved questions (partitions, 4 in a 3P room, lounge purpose)
Gets the next meeting time (Tuesday 2 PM)
weaknesses: Generic 'Speaker 1/3/4' labels make it hard to know who said what
Empty action items section despite clear commitments
Repetitive summary and outline; thin on decisions such as rejecting project-based grouping

evaluations.label: C
errors: 'Susan and Martin both raised concerns about sharing offices' overstates Martin's position; he said he has nothing against sharing
strengths: Accurate and well attributed (Martin warned of zero growth, Susan's confidential rectorate work, Martin's point to speak only for oneself)
Correct owners on action items: Andrei for room separation, Susan for Maggie and Pierrette
Clearly states what is fixed (room count) vs open (assignments), and that no layout was decided
weaknesses: Action items omit checking 4 desks in a 3P room, asking about Gisela with the school admin, and everyone bringing a draft proposal
Gisela options and visitor-in-admin-room objection only briefly covered
Omits MDM morning conflict and amenities

evaluations.label: D
errors: Action item assigns 'Follow up with absent team members (Maggie, Pierrette)' to Andrei; Susan volunteered for this
'Distribute documents of the new office configuration' listed as an action item; it was done during the meeting
'no dedicated cafeteria' contradicts the transcript: there is a cafeteria downstairs that closes at five
'Smoking is allowed only outside, even on balconies' is garbled
'Splitting rooms... currently not feasible due to building and security regulations' overstates; Andre will check
'Project grouping seen as less important than proximity to meeting rooms' is an invented framing
'The session will focus on refining the plan rather than final decisions' is unsupported
'Management recognizes this as a priority due to previously lengthy discussions' is unsupported
strengths: Covers nearly every topic: Gisela options, visitors, smoking, coffee, whiteboards, equipment, 4 in a 3P room
Action list includes most commitments plus the all-participant proposal task
weaknesses: Very long and repetitive (growth, room splitting and admin noise repeated several times)
Several embellishments and one wrong action owner
Timestamps often misplaced, hard to skim for someone who missed the meeting

rationale: A is accurate, complete and has the best next-steps list, losing points only for missing owners and slight overstatement of lounge consensus. C is equally accurate with correct owners but drops several action items. D is comprehensive but verbose, with a wrong owner for the Maggie/Pierrette follow-up and several embellishments. B uses unhelpful speaker numbers, reverses the faculty-sharing point, and lists no action items.
